A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELogitNorm study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the additional rebuttal page in v2. No material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD detection, classification, calibration, and feature-analysis results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds training curves and a full-spectrum OOD evaluation on its final rebuttal page.

M1.justification: The predicted-class selection, average distance to competing decision boundaries, and normalized cross-entropy objective in Equations (6)–(8) remain unchanged. The new implementation listing is additional documentation, not evidence that the underlying training procedure was revised.

E1.justification: The original four ID benchmarks and their semantic OOD datasets are retained. The appended rebuttal adds ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-C, and ImageNet-R in a full-spectrum ImageNet-200 evaluation, substantially broadening coverage to classification under covariate shift alongside semantic OOD detection.

E2.justification: Outlier Exposure, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes an actual comparator in the rebuttal's full-spectrum table alongside Cross-Entropy and LogitNorm. Comparator membership in the original benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The rebuttal introduces a full-spectrum evaluation reporting MSP-based near/far OOD detection together with ID and shifted-data classification accuracy. Its detailed construction is not specified. Existing training budgets, architectures, optimizer settings, detection metrics, and ECE binning remain unchanged; 200-epoch training already appeared in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds ImageNet-200 and CIFAR-100 training-stability curves, computational-overhead analysis, and a covariate-shift robustness check. The original CIFAR-10 curve and feature visualizations are retained after relocation. v1's brief qualitative temperature-sensitivity finding is omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use three different random seeds and report average performance. v2 adds no new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit increase in run counts.

E6.justification: All seven matched result tables retain their numerical entries. Newly reported evidence includes training curves and the full-spectrum table, where ELogitNorm obtains near/far AUROC of 52.29/73.62 and shifted-data accuracy of 44.86. These are additional results under different evaluation conditions, not changes to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The two propositions and their appendix proofs retain the same mathematical substance. Supplement Section 3 adds a limited computational-cost analysis, stating O(C^2 D) complexity for pairwise weight distances and deriving operation-count estimates.

C1.justification: The central claims of hyperparameter-free normalization, reduced feature collapse, improved OOD detection, and preserved classification remain. Compatibility narrows from 'any' post-hoc score in v1's introduction to 'most' in v2. The conclusion replaces explicit acknowledgment of occasional near-OOD degradation with a stronger robustness-and-stability characterization.

C2.justification: v2 removes the specific explanation linking near-OOD failures to inaccurate decision boundaries and emphasizes a general limitation of training-time methods. It newly asserts best calibration regardless of scaling and universal near/far improvements, interpretations contradicted by retained tables. It also adds substantive efficiency explanations and scope discussions concerning wild-data access, ViTs, label noise, and class imbalance.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code URL, a self-contained PyTorch loss listing, and implementation and overhead details in Supplement Section 3. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, the listing averages over all c entries, including the zero self-gap, whereas Equation (7) divides by c−1; this creates an implementation-documentation inconsistency.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded with dedicated calibration and feature-collapse discussions, comparisons to feature-normalization approaches including T2FNorm, and positioning against joint OOD generalization/detection work such as SCONE, AHA, and InfoBound. Earlier likelihood-based preliminaries and some contrastive-learning discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method motivation, results discussion, related work, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Feature-collapse motivation is reorganized into dimensional and origin collapse, discussion topics are reordered, and the appendix becomes separately structured supplementary material with an appended rebuttal.

P2.justification: The visual style and most existing displays are retained. Main Figure 4 changes to an ImageNet-200 training plot, while its original CIFAR-10 plot moves into a supplementary pair with CIFAR-100. v2 adds a code figure and rebuttal table, relocates supplementary displays, and correctly relabels the ID-accuracy display as Table 5.

improvement.justification: The full-spectrum evaluation, broader research positioning, and implementation material improve coverage and inspectability. However, v2 introduces stronger unsupported interpretations: Table 4 still gives raw-logit ECE of 26.7 for ELogitNorm versus 3.3 for Cross-Entropy, contradicting superiority regardless of scaling, and supplementary near-OOD results contradict universal improvement claims. The new code also disagrees with Equation (7)'s averaging factor. These substantive reliability costs make the net quality direction uncertain.
